name: AIPOCH Open-Science
one_liner: Local-first AI research workbench: agents run Python/R, every result keeps provenance

text.why: It gathers research AI work that usually scatters across chat windows, notebooks, scripts and reporting tools into one desktop app. A five-step first run installs Claude Code, OpenCode, Codex or CodeBuddy as the agent runtime (no Node.js or admin password needed) and connects a model via a built-in cloud provider, a custom gateway or a Claude/Codex subscription login. It includes Python and R kernels, literature search across Europe PMC, OpenAlex and arXiv, 24 built-in data connectors and 22 featured skills, and every generated table or figure is kept as an immutable version with checksums, execution history and inputs that can be replayed in an isolated environment for verification. An Electron app for macOS, Windows and Linux; v0.29.0 (2026-09-13), Apache-2.0.
text.take: Its focus is recording where each result came from, with versions and replay verification — while model costs stay separate and prompts plus attached context still go to whichever provider you pick.
build: The headless CLI and Node.js SDK share the desktop's local daemon, projects and permissions, so you could build an unattended pipeline that re-analyses a fixed dataset on a schedule and emits a report with verification records. Custom MCP connectors can bring in an in-house database.

who.role: Computational researchers in bioinformatics, statistics, chemistry
who.situation: agents run code, search literature, produce tables and figures
artifact versions, checksums and replay verification records

start.text: # Windows x64 installer and Linux x64 AppImage/.deb are under Assets on the latest GitHub release
# First run, five steps: Environment → Data location → Agent runtime (Claude Code/OpenCode/Codex/CodeBuddy) → Model provider connection test → Notebook runtime (optional)
# New project → describe goal, input data and how to check the result in a session → run, then open the Provenance view

caveat: Apache-2.0 — the software is free with no seat licence (homepage), and the homepage states it is not affiliated with Anthropic

Model usage is billed separately: built-in cloud providers and custom gateways need your own API key, or reuse a Claude/Codex subscription login; prompts and attached context are sent to the provider you choose
Electron desktop app, v0.29.0 (2026-09-13) — the README says provider lists, catalogs and UI change between versions; the #1 BiomniBench-DA Public 50 claim is the project's own report
